newsitem.title: USA: US Plains cattle market quiet, no sales - feedlots.
newsitem.headline: US Plains cattle market quiet, no sales - feedlots.

text.p: U.S. Plains feedlot cattle markets near midday on Monday were quiet, with no reported trades, feedlot sources said.
Packer bids at $67.00 were passed by owners asking $69.00 to $70.00, they said. The bulk of cattle last week sold at $67.00, with a few late sales at $68.00.
Sales this week were expected at firm prices amid expectations for continued strength in beef prices and strong demand from packers said to be still short of cattle despite last week's purchases.

Fed cattle prices also were seen being underpinned by smaller numbers of market-ready cattle this week. Showlists have been reduced by a combination of active packer buying and severe winter-like weather last week, some sources said.
Also, several owners reportedly pulled cattle ahead to fill packer needs last week, they said.

Cold, snow and ice late last week reportedly impacted weight gains on some cattle in Kansas and Nebraska, which spurred talk owners may keep the cattle on feed another week in an attempt to recoup gains, some cattle feeders said.
However, the weather moderated on Sunday and warm winds reportedly were drying feedyards quickly and improving rates of gain, they said.
